sources: Wikimedia 'On this day' feed, 25 September: Battle of Stamford Bridge

Wikipedia: Battle of Stamford Bridge — 25 September 1066; traditionally the end of the Viking Age; 300 ships (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle) / over 200 (Snorri); Tostig, Harold's brother, with the invaders; London to Yorkshire, about 185 miles, in four days, taking the Norwegians completely by surprise; a lone Norwegian with an axe held the bridge, cut down more than 40 Englishmen, and was killed by a soldier who floated under the bridge and speared him through the planks; Hardrada and Tostig both killed
Wikipedia: Harald Hardrada — King of Norway; 'Thunderbolt of the North' (Adam of Bremen)
Wikipedia: Harold Godwinson — died at the Battle of Hastings, 14 October 1066; succeeded by William the Conqueror

sentences.say: On this day in ten sixty-six, the Viking Age ended at a bridge in Yorkshire. Or so they say.
sentences.show: On this day in 1066, the Viking Age ended at a bridge in Yorkshire. Or so they say.

sentences.say: Harald Hardrada, King of Norway, had invaded England with hundreds of ships.
sentences.show: Harald Hardrada, King of Norway, had invaded England with hundreds of ships.

sentences.say: Fighting at his side was the English king's own brother, Tostig.
sentences.show: Fighting at his side was the English king's own brother, Tostig.

sentences.say: But King Harold marched a hundred and eighty-five miles, in just four days.
sentences.show: But King Harold marched 185 miles, in just four days.

sentences.say: The Vikings never saw him coming.
sentences.show: The Vikings never saw him coming.

sentences.say: At the bridge, one Viking with an axe held back the whole English army.
sentences.show: At the bridge, one Viking with an axe held back the whole English army.

sentences.say: He cut down more than forty men, until a soldier floated under the bridge, and speared him through the planks.
sentences.show: He cut down more than forty men, until a soldier floated under the bridge, and speared him through the planks.

sentences.say: By the end, Hardrada and Tostig were both dead.
sentences.show: By the end, Hardrada and Tostig were both dead.

sentences.say: Nineteen days later, he died at Hastings, and William the Conqueror took the crown.
sentences.show: Nineteen days later, he died at Hastings, and William the Conqueror took the crown.

sentences.say: Every day has a story like this.
sentences.show: Every day has a story like this.
